payload.title: Authorised Marriage Celebrants and Who Can Legally Marry You
payload.excerpt: Who can perform a marriage in Australia is a short list, and it is fixed by law.
key_takeaways: Only an authorised marriage celebrant can legally marry you in Australia, and there are four types.
You can check any Commonwealth-registered celebrant on the official register, which shows their status and whether they are civil or religious.
A friend or family member can only legally marry you once registered as a celebrant, and assessment can take up to 6 months.
An Australian-authorised celebrant cannot perform a marriage overseas, so you either marry legally at home first or follow the destination's own rules.

faq.q: Can a friend legally marry us in Australia?
faq.a: Only once they are registered as an authorised marriage celebrant. Until then they cannot accept a NOIM or solemnise a marriage, and AGD has up to 6 months to assess an application. Ask your celebrant how a friend or family member can take part in the ceremony.

faq.q: What is a marriage celebrant in Australia?
faq.a: An authorised marriage celebrant is a person with legal authority to marry you in Australia. They fall into four types: Commonwealth-registered marriage celebrants, Commonwealth-registered religious marriage celebrants, ministers of religion from a recognised denomination, and state and territory officers.

faq.q: Do you have to be ordained to marry someone in Australia?
faq.a: No. Commonwealth-registered civil celebrants qualify through the Certificate IV in Celebrancy, an approved university qualification or celebrancy skills. To identify as a religious marriage celebrant, however, a person must be a minister of religion.

faq.q: Can a Justice of the Peace marry you in Australia?
faq.a: Only if they are also an authorised marriage celebrant. Being a Justice of the Peace is not one of the four types of authorised celebrant. Check their name on the official register.

faq.q: How long does it take to get legally married in Australia?
faq.a: Your NOIM must reach your celebrant at least 1 month and no more than 18 months before the wedding. In some circumstances a prescribed authority can authorise a shorter notice period.

faq.q: Can our Australian celebrant marry us overseas?
faq.a: No. An Australian-authorised marriage celebrant cannot perform a marriage overseas. Your celebrant can marry you legally in Australia before you leave, or you can marry under the destination's own rules.

faq.q: How do I check if a celebrant is authorised?
faq.a: Search AGD's register at marriage.ag.gov.au by name or state. Each Commonwealth-registered celebrant's entry shows their registration status and whether they perform civil ceremonies or are a religious marriage celebrant.
